title: Release
intent: He finishes, lights the house, and leaves it kept.
emotionalTurn: Leaving lit, not locked in darkness.
openingImage: sands the chair in morning light, dust in the sunbeam
closingImage: walks back down the drive at dusk, slower and lighter, house lit behind him

shots.action: sands the chair in morning light, dust in the sunbeam
shots.lockedLookBlock: Desaturated late-light realism, warm practical lamps against cold blue-grey daylight, muted earth palette of rust, faded denim, worn wood and grey sky, locked-off camera with slow push-ins only, 35mm normal lens feel, soft natural grain, no drone shots, no saturated color.

shots.background: Foreground: workshop bench and sandpaper. Midground: the man sanding the chair in morning light. Deep background: workshop window with morning sun, dust in the sunbeam.
shots.choreography: Beat 1 (0-3s): man sands the chair, slow strokes. Beat 2 (3-7s): dust rises in the sunbeam as he sands. Beat 3, payoff (7-10s): hold on the chair in morning light, dust settling — work finishing, not finished yet.
shots.cameraChoreography: Locked-off: camera does not move, wide framing with the workshop, the chair, and the morning sunbeam in one composition.
shots.lighting: Morning light through the workshop window, warm and clear, dust visible in the sunbeam, rest of the workshop in soft shadow. Morning light here is the release sequence's light, distinct from arrival's golden hour.
shots.focus: Deep focus: man, chair, and sunbeam all sharp.
shots.motion: Subject motion: slow sanding strokes, rhythmic. Background motion: dust in the sunbeam. Camera still — the light, not the camera, moves the shot.
shots.extras: No background performers; the workshop is empty.
shots.loreNotes: Chair rule: sanding is the finishing stage, after gluing in s16 and before the finished chair in s18. Light rule: release in morning light.

departments.production-design: Chair must now be visibly closer to finished — joints set, surfaces smoothed, but not yet the finished chair of s18
departments.costume: Sawdust on jacket and trousers, heaviest here

shots.action: runs a hand over the finished chair and nods once
shots.lockedLookBlock: Desaturated late-light realism, warm practical lamps against cold blue-grey daylight, muted earth palette of rust, faded denim, worn wood and grey sky, locked-off camera with slow push-ins only, 35mm normal lens feel, soft natural grain, no drone shots, no saturated color.

shots.background: Foreground: finished chair edge, smooth wood. Midground: the man's hand running over the finished chair. Deep background: workshop window with morning light, out of focus.
shots.choreography: Beat 1 (0-3s): hand finds the finished chair's rail. Beat 2 (3-7s): hand runs over the finished surface, slowly. Beat 3, payoff (7-10s): man nods once, then a soft exhale, hold on quiet satisfaction — no smile, no celebration, just a nod.
shots.cameraChoreography: Locked-off: camera does not move, close framing on the hand, the chair, and the man's face in profile.
shots.lighting: Morning light on the finished chair, hand in warm light, background in soft shadow.
shots.focus: Shallow focus: hand and chair sharp, man's face slightly soft in profile.
shots.motion: Subject motion: hand running, nod, exhale — the smallest possible celebration. Background motion: dust settling in morning light. Camera still.
shots.extras: No background performers; the workshop is empty.
shots.loreNotes: Chair rule: finished here, for the first time. The nod is the film's quietest climax — it must not be played as triumph, only as satisfaction.

departments.production-design: Finished chair must be the same chair as s10-s17, now with a finished surface, same wood, same proportions
departments.costume: Jacket with sawdust, hands on finished wood
departments.sound: Silence, then a soft exhale — the exhale is the sound cue, not music

shots.background: Foreground: garden gate and gatepost, morning light on worn paint. Midground: the man at the gate. Deep background: garden path and drive in morning light, birdsong audible.
shots.choreography: Beat 1 (0-3s): man reaches the gate from the house side. Beat 2 (3-7s): he opens the gate to morning light. Beat 3, payoff (7-10s): he stands in the open gate, looking out, hold on opening, not closing — the reverse of s02.
shots.cameraChoreography: Push-in: from a wide shot at 4 metres to a closer framing at 2 metres, ending with the man in the open gate and morning light behind him.
shots.lighting: Morning light, clear and warm, gate wood lit, garden in bright light — the reverse of s02's fading golden hour.
shots.focus: Focus on the man and the gate, garden and drive slightly soft behind.
shots.motion: Subject motion: reach, open, stand — the reverse threshold of s02. Background motion: garden in morning light, birds. Camera pushes in steadily.
shots.extras: No background performers; the garden is empty at this moment.
shots.loreNotes: Gate rule: s19 is the reverse of s02 — opening, not closing, morning, not dusk. The gate must be the same gate, same paint, same post.

departments.production-design: Gate is the same gate as s02, now in morning light
departments.costume: Jacket unchanged, boots on the path

shots.background: Foreground: garden path gravel and edging stones. Midground: the man walking the garden path. Deep background: garden fence and a neighbour at the fence, waving, out of focus.
shots.choreography: Beat 1 (0-3s): man walks the garden path, slowly. Beat 2 (3-7s): neighbour waves from the fence; man returns the wave, briefly, without stopping. Beat 3, payoff (7-10s): man continues walking, hold on rejoining the world, briefly — not a reunion, just a wave.
shots.cameraChoreography: Tracking: camera tracks with the man along the path at his pace, ending in a medium shot with the fence and neighbour behind him.
shots.lighting: Morning light on the path and garden, neighbour in soft light at the fence, no artificial light.
shots.focus: Focus on the man, neighbour slightly soft at the fence — the wave is brief, not a scene.
shots.motion: Subject motion: walk, wave, walk on — the wave does not stop the walk. Background motion: garden in morning light. Camera tracks, then holds.
shots.extras: One background performer: a neighbour at the garden fence, waving once, not approaching, not speaking at length.
shots.loreNotes: World rule: rejoining the world, briefly. The neighbour is not a new character with a story; the wave is the whole relationship in this film.

departments.production-design: Garden fence and path must match s02/s19's garden, same gate system
departments.sound: Footsteps on gravel, a distant voice, no music

shots.background: Foreground: porch boards and a broom, worn bristles. Midground: the man sweeping the porch. Deep background: garden and drive in morning light, out of focus.
shots.choreography: Beat 1 (0-3s): man sweeps the porch, slow strokes. Beat 2 (3-7s): he sweeps methodically, covering the porch in order. Beat 3, payoff (7-10s): hold on the swept porch — care as a closing act, the house kept, not just visited.
shots.cameraChoreography: Locked-off: camera does not move, medium framing with the porch, the broom, and the man in one composition.
shots.lighting: Morning light on the porch boards, broom and dust in warm light, garden behind in bright light.
shots.focus: Focus on the man and the broom, porch boards sharp, garden soft.
shots.motion: Subject motion: slow, methodical sweeping, one stroke per few seconds. Background motion: dust moving with the broom. Camera still — method is the beat.
shots.extras: No background performers; the porch is empty.
shots.loreNotes: House rule: empty but kept, dust not ruin. Sweeping the porch is the keeping, made visible — it is not cleaning for a visitor, it is care.

departments.production-design: Porch boards, rail, and door must match s03's porch
departments.costume: Jacket unchanged, boots on porch boards

shots.action: switches on the porch light at dusk

shots.background: Foreground: porch wall and light switch, worn plate. Midground: the man's hand reaching for the switch. Deep background: porch and garden at dusk, out of focus.
shots.choreography: Beat 1 (0-3s): hand reaches for the porch light switch. Beat 2 (3-7s): hand switches the light on, click audible. Beat 3, payoff (7-10s): hold on the porch light glowing warm at dusk — the house left lit, the film's central image, switched on deliberately.
shots.cameraChoreography: Locked-off: camera does not move, close framing on the switch, the hand, and the light fixture, so the click and the glow read as one beat.
shots.lighting: Dusk light fading, porch light warm and glowing from the fixture, hand in warm light, garden darkening behind.
shots.focus: Focus on the switch and fixture, hand sharp, garden blurred.
shots.motion: Subject motion: reach, switch, hold — the smallest action with the largest meaning. Background motion: dusk darkening. Camera still.
shots.extras: No background performers; the porch is empty.
shots.loreNotes: Porch light rule: switched on here at dusk, left on in s23-s24. The house is left lit, not locked in darkness. Turning it off would reverse the film's meaning.

departments.production-design: Porch light fixture must be the same fixture as s03's unlit fixture
departments.sound: Switch click, warm lamp hum, no music

shots.background: Foreground: window frame from outside, dusk light on glass. Midground: the finished chair inside the window, lit from inside. Deep background: house interior warm light, porch light glow at the frame edge.
shots.choreography: Beat 1 (0-3s): man places the finished chair in the window, carefully. Beat 2 (3-7s): he steps back, leaving the chair in the window. Beat 3, payoff (7-10s): hold on the chair in the window, lit from inside — the work kept, visible, not hidden away.
shots.cameraChoreography: Locked-off: camera does not move, wide framing from outside the window, with the chair, the window, and the house's warm light in one composition.
shots.lighting: Dusk outside, warm lamp light inside, chair lit from inside, window glass catching the dusk.
shots.focus: Focus on the chair in the window, house interior slightly soft behind it.
shots.motion: Subject motion: place, step back, hold. Background motion: evening light fading outside, lamp light steady inside. Camera still — the chair, not the man, is the subject of the hold.
shots.extras: No background performers; the house is empty except for the man placing the chair.
shots.loreNotes: Chair rule: finished chair, placed in the window, lit from inside. The work is kept and visible — not stored, not hidden, not given away in this film.

departments.production-design: Window must be the same window as s08's kitchen window system, but the chair in it is the finished workshop chair, placed deliberately

shots.choreography: Beat 1 (0-3s): man walks back down the drive, slower and lighter than in s01. Beat 2 (3-7s): he continues down the drive, house lit behind him growing smaller in frame. Beat 3, payoff (7-10s): hold on the man walking away with the house lit behind him — release, not departure, the house left lit, not abandoned.
shots.cameraChoreography: Pull-back: camera pulls back slowly from a wide shot to an extreme wide shot, ending with the man small on the drive and the lit house behind him.
shots.lighting: Dusk light fading, house lit warm from inside and by the porch light, man in silhouette against the lit house, sky darkening.
shots.focus: Deep focus: man, drive, and lit house all sharp, so the rhyme with s01 reads — same drive, same house, now lit.
shots.motion: Subject motion: slow walk away, lighter than s01. Background motion: dusk darkening, house light steady. Camera pulls back, the only large camera move in the film's ending, matching the release.
shots.extras: No background performers; the drive is empty except for the man.
shots.loreNotes: Release rule: walks back down the drive at dusk, slower and lighter, house lit behind him. This is the reverse of s01's arrival, with the light changed — the film's final image is a lit house, not a dark one.

departments.production-design: Drive and house must match s01 exactly, except for the light: dark in s01, lit in s24
